criteria_results.title: §2(a): Restore 'entitlement order' language
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly reinserts and defines “Entitlement Order” in Section 1 and restores it in Section 2.2 alongside the Article 9 instruction language, including Bank’s obligation to comply without further Depositor consent. This rejects the Bank’s substitution and preserves the UCC Article 8 control framework.

criteria_results.title: Cover note explains §2(a) entitlement order position
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses the entitlement-order versus instruction terminology, states that Pinnacle restores the rejected entitlement-order language alongside Article 9 instruction language, and explains that the Article 8 reference preserves corresponding control protection if an account is characterized as a securities account.

criteria_results.title: §2(b): Address springing exclusive control and reject broad Bank carve-out
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline preserves springing exclusive control upon receipt of a NOEC and expressly narrows the Bank's carve-out. Sections 2.5 and 3 provide that Graycliff may operate the accounts only before NOEC; after receipt, no new Depositor instructions may be accepted, and only instructions originated and accepted before receipt may be processed during the limited wind-down period.

criteria_results.title: §3: Reject Bank set-off priority over Secured Party instructions
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects Bank set-off priority and restores Secured Party priority. Section 4.1 provides that Secured Party instructions and entitlement orders control in any conflict and prohibits Bank set-off from overriding that priority. Sections 5.1–5.3 further subordinate and narrowly limit the Bank's set-off rights, including after NOEC receipt.

criteria_results.title: §4: Narrow expanded self-help set-off to direct, liquidated obligations
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline rejects the Bank’s broad set-off for any direct or contingent obligation and limits set-off to direct, matured, liquidated, undisputed obligations arising under the applicable deposit-account agreements, with narrow exceptions for customary documented account fees, service/per-item charges, and returned or reversed items.

criteria_results.title: §5: Propose 3-business-day NOEC compliance period
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline changes the Bank's five-business-day NOEC compliance period to three Business Days following receipt and authentication, without reverting to the original two-day period. Although the operative provision is numbered Section 3.5 rather than §5, it expressly proposes the required three-business-day period, and the disposition summary and cover note confirm the same position.

criteria_results.title: §6: Reject indemnification coverage for Bank gross negligence
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects indemnification for losses arising from the Bank's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Section 6.2 excludes gross negligence, willful misconduct, bad faith, and material breach, and Sections 6.3–6.4 similarly preserve those exclusions.

criteria_results.title: §7(a): Reject $50,000 aggregate liability cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects and deletes the $50,000 aggregate liability cap in §7.1, and the disposition summary and cover note confirm that no arbitrary aggregate cap is accepted.

criteria_results.title: §7(b): Address mutual consequential/punitive/indirect damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly addresses §7(b) by retaining and qualifying the mutual waiver of consequential, punitive, and indirect damages. It clarifies that the waiver does not limit direct damages, including misapplied funds, or indemnification obligations, and the cover note explains and reserves Pinnacle's position.

criteria_results.title: Cover note confirms position on §7(b) mutual damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses §7(b), stating that Pinnacle does not require deletion of the mutual consequential, punitive, and indirect damages waiver for this turn, while qualifying acceptance by preserving direct damages and indemnification obligations and reserving the right to revisit the provision.

criteria_results.title: §8: Reject 90-day lookback; propose full subordination or 180-day lookback
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly rejects the Bank's 90-day lookback and replaces it with a 180-day period in Section 5.2. The disposition summary and cover note also consistently state the 180-day counterproposal, satisfying the minimum required lookback.

criteria_results.title: §9: Reject 30-day unilateral termination; propose 90-day notice with transition rights
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9 rejects the Bank’s 30-day unilateral termination right and replaces it with 90 days’ prior written notice, continued compliance during the notice period, replacement-account and replacement-ACA transition protections, and no termination until the Secured Party confirms replacement control arrangements are in place.

criteria_results.title: §10: Restore New York governing law
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.1 expressly deletes “North Carolina” and inserts “New York” as the governing law. The disposition summary and cover note likewise state that the Bank’s North Carolina change is rejected and New York law is restored.

criteria_results.title: Cover note acknowledges New York governing law is strongly preferred with possible flexibility
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses governing law and states that Pinnacle restores New York law and New York courts because they align with the Credit Agreement and other Loan Documents. This clearly indicates New York is the preferred position, even though it does not expressly offer flexibility if Ironbridge treats the issue as a deal-breaker.

criteria_results.title: §12: Restore no-prior-control-agreement representation
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 12.1 restores the Bank’s representations that no other person has control over the Accounts, that the Bank has not entered into and will not enter into another control agreement without the Secured Party’s consent, and that the Bank has received no notice of any other lien, claim, interest, or adverse claim.

criteria_results.title: §13: Restore successor-bank notification obligation
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline restores the successor-bank notification obligation. Section 8.1 requires the Bank to provide the Secured Party at least 30 days’ prior written notice before transferring the Accounts or its obligations, or undergoing a merger, consolidation, or transfer to a successor bank, and also includes successor-assumption and continuity protections.

criteria_results.title: §11: Accept annual maintenance fee but negotiate down $15,000 legal-fee reimbursement
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.1 accepts the $3,500 per-account annual maintenance fee ($10,500 total), while Section 11.2 rejects the $15,000 legal-fee reimbursement and caps it at the lesser of $7,500 or actual reasonable, documented costs.

criteria_results.title: Cover note references May 30, 2025 perfection deadline

criteria_results.title: Cover note conveys urgency and encourages prompt turnaround

All three parties are also correctly reflected in the account schedule and signature blocks.

criteria_results.title: ACA maintains form and substance satisfactory to Administrative Agent
criteria_results.reasoning: The counter-markup preserves Article 9 control by requiring the Bank to comply with Secured Party instructions without further Depositor consent, restores Article 8 entitlement-order language where applicable, bars new Depositor instructions after a NOEC, gives Secured Party instructions priority, and narrowly limits and subordinates Bank set-off rights. It does not accept any Bank change that would materially undermine valid control or perfection.

criteria_results.title: Cover note maintains professional and cordial tone
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note is formal, respectful, and appropriately cordial for inter-counsel negotiations. It clearly and firmly explains Pinnacle’s positions and rationale without becoming adversarial, and it closes constructively by inviting further discussion and emphasizing timely resolution.
